curatorBrief.title: Welcome to the World of Addition!
curatorBrief.intent: Welcome young mathematicians to addition! Introduce the adventure of putting groups of objects together, discovering the math symbols plus and equal, and seeing how combining things makes bigger numbers.

objectiveBlocks.objectiveText: Combine two groups of physical objects to find the total amount

components.title: Story Time: Bringing Friends Together
components.intent: Guide kindergarteners through an interactive story scene where they act out joining two small groups of objects, like ducks joining a pond, to count the combined total.

components.title: Fill the Frame: Putting Groups Together
components.intent: Allow students to place counters into a ten-frame to physically see and count how two distinct groups combine to create one total amount within 10.

components.title: Count the Whole Group
components.intent: Encourage students to practice one-to-one counting on a collection of playful items created by joining two separate clusters, saying the total count aloud.

objectiveBlocks.objectiveText: Identify the plus sign (+) and equal sign (=) as math symbols

components.title: Meet the Math Symbols: Plus and Equal
components.intent: Introduce the plus sign (+) as the symbol that puts things together and the equal sign (=) as the symbol that shows what both sides have in total, supported by simple visual cards.

components.title: Building Number Sentences
components.intent: Invite students to place the plus sign and equal sign into scaffolded slots between object groups and numerals to build a complete math sentence.

objectiveBlocks.objectiveText: Explain how putting things together makes a bigger number

components.title: Part-Part-Whole: Growing Bigger
components.intent: Show how two smaller part circles join branches into one larger whole circle, helping students visually understand that combining amounts results in a bigger quantity.

components.title: Comparing Before and After
components.intent: Provide side-by-side visual comparisons of an initial group versus the new, combined group to reinforce that putting more items in makes the total group larger.

components.title: Roll, Combine, and Grow
components.intent: Have students roll two dice, observe each individual pip pattern, and speak the bigger combined sum aloud with supportive direct instruction feedback.

finalAssessment.title: Addition Superstar Check
finalAssessment.intent: Assess kindergarten understanding across all three objectives: combining two sets of objects, recognizing '+' and '=', and recognizing that combining amounts yields a bigger number.

problems.question: What is 2 red apples and 3 green apples in all?
problems.rationale: When you combine 2 red apples and 3 green apples, you count all of them together to get 5. Starting with 2 and counting 3 more (3, 4, 5) gives a total of 5 apples.
problems.teachingNote: Encourage students to use concrete counters or fingers to model joining two separate sets into one combined group.
successCriteria: Combine two sets of objects to find the total quantity up to 5.
Recognize that adding 2 and 3 results in 5.
problems.subject: MATHEMATICS

problems.question: What math sign means to put things together?
problems.rationale: The plus sign shows addition, which means putting groups together to make more. When we see a plus sign, we combine things into one bigger group. The minus sign is used for taking things away instead.
problems.teachingNote: Use physical manipulatives like counting blocks or fingers when introducing the plus sign so students can physically bring two groups together as they say 'plus'.
successCriteria: Identify the plus sign as the symbol used for joining or adding groups.
problems.subject: MATHEMATICS

problems.question: Start at 2 and jump forward 2 steps. Where do you land?
problems.rationale: Starting at 2 and moving forward 2 hops lands on 4. Each jump counts forward one more number: 2 plus 1 is 3, and one more hop makes 4. So, 2 + 2 = 4!
problems.teachingNote: Encourage kindergarteners to use their fingers to trace hops along the line, counting each hop aloud ('one hop to 3, two hops to 4').
successCriteria: Use a number line to add two numbers within 5
Identify the landing number after jumping forward
problems.subject: MATHEMATICS

problems.statement: When you put 2 toys and 1 toy together, you get a bigger number of toys.
problems.rationale: When we combine groups of objects, like putting 2 toys together with 1 toy, the total amount grows to become a bigger number. This is the basic idea of addition, which means joining groups to find out how many there are in all.
problems.teachingNote: Use physical toys or counting blocks to let students physically combine groups so they can see and feel that the total count increases.
successCriteria: Understand that combining groups increases the total amount
Recognize addition as putting things together
